title: Gas prices are high right now. Use these 6 tools to save on fuel
raw_text:
Just ahead of summer road trip season, Americans are feeling even more pain at the pump.
The national average price for a gallon of regular gas hit $4.39 on May 1, according to AAA. That's an increase of about 8% from a month earlier, when gas reached $4.06 per gallon.
Americans aren't just feeling price hikes in gas; they're seeing increases for other essentials like food. But there are ways to find cheaper gas, if you know where to look and what tools to use. Below, CNBC Select rounds up our top ways to save on gas.
There's never been a better time to shop around before you fill up the tank. Gas prices can vary widely, even from block to block. Keeping an eye on prices can help, but comparing numbers across a large area can help you find better deals.
GasBuddy can help you view prices at dozens of local stations, allowing you to filter by price, distance or both factors. It's free to download and use, and available in both the Apple App Store and the Google Play Store. The app can also help you earn rewards for completing tasks like uploading receipts.
Features
Gasbuddy helps you find the cheapest gas near you in one easy-to-use app. It's helped people find the best gas prices over 900 million times and save over $3.1 billion at the pump.
App availability
Available in both the Apple App Store and the Google Play store
Price
Free
Many wholesale clubs like Costco, Sam's Club and BJ's offer gas at more affordable prices than standard gas stations. However, the low prices aren't accessible to everyone — you'll need to be a member of the club. Prices can vary between clubs, so make sure to compare costs in advance.
Consider the math: memberships for Sam's Club's and Costco Gold Star — both of which give customers access to gas — are $60 and $65, respectively. BJ's Club+ membership is $120 annually. Most cars hold between 12 and 16 gallons of gas, and with prices at $4.39, you'd spend at least $50 at the pump filling up your tank once.
Plus, memberships can be combined with the brands' credit cards to earn rewards.
The Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi has no annual fee for Costco members and earns 5% cash back on Costco gas, plus 4% on other eligible gas and electric vehicle (EV) charging (up to $7,000 in combined spending per year, then 1%). You'll also earn rewards on eligible travel and restaurant purchases, plus 2% back at Costco and Costco.com.
The Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi is a valuable card to pair with a Costco membership, but the rewards program is more restrictive than what you get with a typical cash-back card.

An Amazon Prime membership can also help you save. Prime members get $0.10 off per gallon through Amazon's partnership with earnify™, the loyalty program from BP and its subsidiaries.
Additionally, now through May 29, members can get $0.20 off per gallon on one fill-up every Friday at BP and Amoco, along with participating ampm and Thorntons locations across the U.S.
To get started, create your earnify™ account, activate your membership at amazon.com/fuelsavings, and pair the two accounts. Then, you'll be able to use your phone number or a linked payment method to get the discount. However, this discount only applies at qualifying gas stations, so review the list of stations near you and make sure to compare prices at those stations ahead of time.

This promotion doesn't require you to use a certain credit card to qualify but you can make the deal even better with credit cards that offer cash back on fuel. The Prime Visa is only available to Amazon Prime members ($139 for an annual membership and $14.99 for a monthly membership) but is very rewarding for Amazon purchases.

Credit cards aren't just a way to pay for the things you buy every day — they're also a way to get rewarded.
Some cards offer higher rewards levels for rotating categories, while others offer a flat percentage of cash back or even travel points for the purchases you make.
If you spend a lot on fuel and want to maximize your earnings, the Citi Custom Cash® Card could be a strong option. This card has no annual fee, and cardholders earn 5% cash back on one of 10 top eligible spend categories each billing cycle (on up to $500 in spending, then 1%). If gas stations are your highest spending category for that cycle, you'll earn 5% cash back, one of the best rates we've seen.
The Citi Custom Cash® Card is an especially simple and rewarding cash back card because you'll automatically earn bonus rewards where you spend the most.

If you're already an AAA member — or thinking of joining for the discounts on travel-related items and services — you could find deals.
AAA members can save at eligible Shell gas stations by signing up for the free Shell Fuel Rewards® program. As a member, you'll save $0.30 per gallon on your first fill-up. Then, you'll save $0.05 off per gallon on up to 20 gallons at participating Shell stations.
Some gas stations will offer a small discount for using cash — typically between $0.05 and $0.10 off per gallon, according to NerdWallet. While that might seem like a small amount, it could add up if you have a large gas tank or buy gas frequently.
Ask your local stations if they offer a discount for those paying in cash. If they do, keeping some cash could help you get that discount. Having easy ATM access could also help you take advantage of a cash discount.
The Axos Bank CashBack Checking Account includes free withdrawals from over 95,000 ATMs nationwide, plus unlimited reimbursements for any out-of-network machines you might encounter domestically in the U.S. It also doesn't have any monthly maintenance fees and offers 1% cash back on purchases requiring a signature, a feature many other debit cards don't have.
